External state information and incentives can mislead reinforcement learning agents, causing them to learn incorrect behaviors. To address this issue, we introduce a novel approach to uncover and eliminate external state information and incentives that are not part of the task at hand. Our approach identifies and removes latent variables that are unobserved but influence the system's dynamics. By doing so, we can guarantee that the optimal policy derived from our approach matches the optimal policy in the original Markov decision process. We also introduce a new metric to quantify the unobserved external state information and incentives, and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through both simulation and real-world experiments.

The blockchain-based smart contract technology is being utilized to automate transactions and agreements, with the potential to automate complex, multi-party arrangements. This paper presents a novel approach to validating blockchain-based smart contracts by integrating refinement types with a Coq-based tool, specifically applied to the Tezos blockchain. To address the intricacies of Tezos' smart contract language, Michelson, this work proposes a more expressive intermediate language and proves its semantic equivalence to Michelson through refinement soundness. As a result, developers can formally verify the correctness of their smart contracts in Michelson by refining intermediate language programs, with the added benefit of leveraging the modular compositionality of the refinement type system. The approach is demonstrated with a case study on the Tezos protocol's protocol parameter module, with the source code available on GitHub.

A graph convolutional neural network (GCNN) variant, known as spectral mixing, can be understood through a matched filter perspective. This perspective reveals that spectral mixing essentially matches a graph signal's frequency components with those of the graph itself. By applying this matched filter interpretation, we can derive an unbiased estimator for graph Fourier transforms, which in turn enables the development of an information-theoretic measure for graph frequency domain mutual information. Furthermore, GCNN architectures can be optimally designed by maximizing mutual information, leading to significant performance enhancements. In particular, our proposed method yields an optimal linear GCNN that surpasses conventional approaches in both accuracy and computational efficiency.

We develop a Chern-Simons-like theory for Einstein's general relativity that includes a scalar field, using a specific type of symmetry-breaking pattern. Through this, we derive a set of equations that describe how these fields behave in the presence of gravity. We then use these equations to analyze stationary, axisymmetric objects in the form of black holes and solitons. In our study, we focus on objects that have a type of hair made of spinning fields. Our results show that these hairy objects can be created by starting with a type of object that has been broken in a way that changes its symmetry. Our findings also provide a way to understand the relationship between the mass of these objects and the amount of hair they have, as well as the amount of angular momentum they possess. We also explore the possibility of finding objects that have the same mass and angular momentum but different amounts of hair, a phenomenon known as multi-degeneracy. Our research is supported by a diagram that shows the relationship between the amount of hair these objects have and the amount of angular momentum they possess, as well as a diagram that shows the possible configurations of these objects in a way that is similar to the way we see the sky.

We observe that in theories featuring SU(N) gauge groups and hypermultiplets, there's a connection to non-analytic symmetries under specific conditions. Specifically, when the number of colors is an odd number greater than three, this symmetry corresponds to the presence of D3-branes within the Calabi-Yau four-fold space. Conversely, when the number of colors is even, the symmetry is related to orientifold D3-branes. The breaking of this U(1) R-symmetry is represented by the non-zero vacuum expectation values of certain fields, which are analogous to D3-brane positions in the internal space. The resulting superpotential, which is an N=2 theory with perturbative corrections, is determined by the moduli space of the gauge theory, which is influenced by the geometry of the space in which the branes reside. The non-perturbative corrections to the moduli space are related to the Gopakumar-Vafa invariants, which are determined by the counting of instantons. The relationship between the mirror toric three-fold and the original toric three-fold is established through a mirror transformation, which is determined by the periods of the holomorphic three-form. In ultrasound elastography, estimating lateral shifts accurately is crucial for generating high-resolution images. However, conventional methods that use virtual sources to calculate the phase of received signals suffer from inaccuracies due to the assumption of linear propagation. These methods fail to consider the curved paths that sound waves actually follow. A new approach called the virtual origin (VOS) method has been developed to overcome this limitation by calculating the actual distance between the source and the receiver. Our research shows that the VOS method provides more precise distance calculations, resulting in higher phase measurement accuracy. The VOS method was implemented using a virtual source that is located at the actual source position, and the accuracy of the phase measurements was improved by up to 30%. The VOS method was also tested on simulated data and demonstrated elastographic lateral shift estimation accuracy of less than 0.02 mm, which is comparable to the state-of-the-art methods. The VOS method is a simple and effective approach that can be used to improve the accuracy of ultrasound elastography images.

Automated generation of demonstrations for the efficient solving of optimization problems is a well-established technique. These demonstrations, often used in the context of algorithms, provide optimal solutions and are an integral part of understanding algorithmic effectiveness. However, the connection between an algorithm's performance and the solution it produces is not always clear. To address this issue, we propose a new framework for analyzing algorithms, which incorporates the concept of cost as a fundamental property of both problems and solutions. This framework, which we refer to as rational pseudocode, provides a unified approach to evaluating algorithmic efficiency and demystifies the workings of popular optimization techniques such as gradient descent and the simplex method. By representing algorithms as sequences of cost-reducing operations, rational pseudocode enables a deeper understanding of algorithmic behavior and facilitates the comparison of different approaches. This framework is illustrated through the application of gradient descent to linear regression and the simplex method to linear programming.

A Boolean algebra $B_n$ consists of all subsets of $\{1, 2,..., n\}$ under the operations of union and set difference. When these operations are replaced with union and intersection, $B_n$ becomes a Boolean lattice. This study investigates the structural properties of $V$-shaped posets within Boolean algebras and lattices. We define a Boolean $V$-coloring as a partition of $B_n$ into two sets based on whether an element is 'white' or 'red'. A 2-colored Boolean algebra or lattice is considered 'Ramsey' if it contains a white chain of size 2 or a red antichain of size $v$. The minimal integer 'ramsey number' for a $V$-shaped poset in a 2-colored Boolean algebra or lattice is the smallest $n$ for which a white chain of 2 or a red antichain of $v$ is guaranteed to exist. We determine the minimal 'ramsey number' for a $V$-shaped poset in a 2-colored Boolean algebra or lattice for various values of $v$.

In recent years, high-dimensional data streams have become increasingly common, prompting the development of online learning techniques for learning linear information representations. This paper addresses the challenge of dynamic $k$-means clustering in such data streams, where clusters can change, and the number of cluster centers and their dimensions can be adjusted. We present a novel algorithm that utilizes a limited number of summaries to achieve a competitive competitive ratio in terms of cluster size, center count, and dimensionality. Specifically, our method has a competitive ratio of $O(\max\{k^{1/3}, D^{1/3}\}^2)$, making it the first method to have a competitive ratio that decreases with respect to $k$ and $D$. We also provide an improved analysis of the baseline method, and our new algorithm matches its competitive ratio of $O(k^{2/3})$ when the dimensionality is fixed.

We investigated a stochastic pursuit-evasion game in an n-dimensional space, where both players can choose to leave the space at any time. Given that the players can select a higher dimension for the space, we proved that there exists a point in the hierarchy of these games corresponding to the optimal strategy for the original problem. If the dimension of the space is limited, we found that there is a set of n-dimensional hierarchies where the game is equivalent to the original one.

A likelihood function is considered circular if it satisfies the condition that for any set of alternatives, the likelihood of one alternative given another is equal to the likelihood of the second given the first. Conversely, a likelihood function is nontransitive if the condition that the likelihood of one alternative given a third is at least as great as the likelihood of the second given the third does not always hold. We have developed a method to create circular, transitive likelihood functions using the Fermat-Weber point, and demonstrated through the use of a specific example that there are also nontransitive, circular likelihood functions. Furthermore, we explored the concept of circular, transitive likelihood functions in the context of economic applications.

Low-dose computed tomography (CT) scans offer significant advantages over conventional high-dose CT scans, reducing patient radiation exposure while maintaining diagnostic image quality. However, low-dose CT images often suffer from poor soft-tissue contrast and excessive noise, compromising their diagnostic utility. Our research focuses on improving the noise reduction capabilities of low-dose CT images, particularly for abdominal imaging. We identified limitations in existing unsupervised learning methods, such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which struggle to generate high-quality soft tissue structures. To address this challenge, we proposed a novel approach called AdaSwitch-NET, an AdaIN-switched Cyclic GAN architecture. This model incorporates adaptive instance normalization and multiple generator-discriminator pairs to create more realistic soft tissue structures. Experimental results demonstrate that AdaSwitch-NET outperforms existing unsupervised learning methods, achieving a 10% improvement in peak signal-to-noise ratio and a 15% improvement in structural similarity index.

Conversational agents are becoming increasingly popular due to their ability to interact with users in real-time. To enhance the capabilities of these virtual assistants, researchers have been developing advanced NLP techniques, including pre-training models on large-scale datasets and combining multiple models for better performance. In this paper, we introduce a new semi-supervised contrastive pre-training approach called SPACE-2, which incorporates contrastive learning and tree-structured data augmentation. Our method achieves impressive results in dialog comprehension tasks, surpassing the best current models by a significant margin. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multiple techniques, such as contrastive learning and tree-structured data augmentation, in improving dialog comprehension performance. Our code is available on GitHub.

This research paper introduces the concept of conformal Ricci-Yamabe solitons in ideal fluid spacetimes and examines several properties associated with harmonic, shrinking, and expanding conformal Ricci-Yamabe solitons. Additionally, it proves that when the potential vector field is a timelike, irrational, and expanding field, a conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton cannot exist. The paper also demonstrates the non-existence of a compact harmonic scalar curvature function in a harmonic conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton when the potential vector field is a timelike, irrational field. Furthermore, it shows that a harmonic, expanding soliton cannot exist when the potential vector field is a timelike, irrational field. The paper includes an example of a hypersurface in a standard ideal fluid spacetime that satisfies the conditions of a non-trivial, expanding conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton.

Research on the decoupling effects in the spins of distorted halo nuclei is being investigated. This phenomenon, where the spins of the core are isolated from external influences due to weak coupling, can be studied through the analysis of the total halo nucleus spins and the core spins. Calculations based on the distorted wave coupled-cluster model were performed for $^{11}\mathrm{Be}$ and $^{19}\mathrm{Ne}$, considering their ground and excited states. It was found that the magnetic dipole moments in these states are primarily influenced by the spins of the halo neutron, with minimal impact from the core. This finding holds true for both non-spinning and spinning distorted halo nuclei. Additionally, the degree of spin distortion in the ground state of $^{11}\mathrm{Be}$ was determined to be around 0.3-0.4, with the estimated value of the mixing ratio being approximately 0.3-0.4 eb.

The BasicVSR model has achieved significant success in video super-resolution tasks due to its versatile nature. To further enhance its performance, we introduce an improved version called BasicVSR++, which incorporates several key improvements. Firstly, we introduce transmission-based modules, including texture transmission and structure transmission modules, to better preserve high-frequency details and overall alignment. To overcome the transmission modules' limited feature extraction capabilities, we integrate two attention-based modules: a long-term attention module to capture temporal information and a cross-feature attention module to facilitate effective feature fusion. These enhancements have yielded impressive results, with BasicVSR++ outperforming the original BasicVSR model by a substantial margin, including a 0.55 dB gain in VSRNTUV4K performance.

The CMS experiment at the LHC has observed a significant pattern in muon scattering data, characterized by the emission of vector bosons such as photons and weak bosons. To accurately study this phenomenon, a new algorithm has been developed to identify and classify these virtual bosons, enhancing the precision of classification by 10-20% compared to previous methods. This improvement is achieved through a combination of machine learning techniques, specifically a decision tree and a neural network, and is validated using muon scattering data collected during 2016-2018. The results indicate that the new algorithm can effectively classify photons with 85% precision and W bosons with 75% precision.

Our research focuses on enhancing the scalability of reinforcement learning (RL) agents operating in complex, real-world environments that demand adaptation to novel situations. We contend that a single unified policy is not the optimal solution for handling multiple tasks due to conflicting learning objectives and the difficulty of generalizing across diverse tasks. Instead, we propose a two-part system consisting of task-specific modules and a central hub, where each module learns a distinct task and manages a localized task range. When confronted with an unfamiliar task, the system can either delegate to a suitable module or engage the central hub to learn from a broader spectrum of experiences. We have applied this framework to multi-task RL in dynamic mazes, demonstrating that it outperforms a single unified policy by efficiently managing experience through channeling and by preventing interference among tasks.

This paper proposes a novel discrete approximation technique for a class of nonlinear partial differential equations, specifically those involving the porous medium operator on a bounded domain within a complete, non-compact metric space. The underlying metric space is assumed to have a compact boundary. We employ discrete functions to approximate the porous medium operator within a bounded domain. The underlying metric space is not required to have a doubling property or a specific heat flow. The proposed discrete approximation technique is then used to establish regularity properties for the heat flow generated by the porous medium operator on the bounded domain. The resulting regularity results are of local nature and hold true for a broader class of metric measure spaces than those previously considered in existing literature.

We synthesize the seminal ideas of Godel, Tarski, Carnap, and Rosser into a unified framework, known as the GTCR theory of types. This framework expands Godel's type system by incorporating Tarski's semantic approach to truth, redefining logical predicates as semantically distinguishable from non-logical ones. By doing so, we reclassify the symbols of Godel's type system into semantically identifiable and non-identifiable subsets. This modification enables us to reinterpret Godel's first and second theorems, as well as Rosser's first theorem, within the context of the type system. Furthermore, we incorporate Tarski's definition of truth, Carnap's theory of descriptions, and uniform reflection principles into the language of each type. By comparing the expressive power of semantically identifiable predicates with that of non-identifiable ones, we establish the relationship between diagonal lemmas, generalized diagonal lemmas, and the Tarski-Godel sentence. This formalization of the type system provides a unified framework for understanding the interplay between these key concepts in mathematical logic.

This paper extends the concept of index theory for Dirac operators on a three-dimensional boundary to identify interior Dirac eigenvalues. Building on previous work by several researchers, we apply a three-spheres theorem for entire functions in a bounded domain in R3 to establish the discrete nature of a set of radii, which in turn helps prove the finiteness of eigenspaces and the discrete character of the Dirac eigenvalue spectrum within that domain.

Consecutive sampling is a systematic approach to sampling that generates a sequence of samples from an underlying population. The approach is used to estimate population parameters and can be applied in various contexts. The {Consecutive Spatially Equitable} sampling approach is a new method that combines the benefits of the {Consecutive} and {Spatially Equitable} sampling approaches. The {Consecutive Spatially Equitable} approach is designed to select a sequence of samples from a geographic area in an equitable manner. The {Consecutive} approach is used to select a sequence of samples, while the {Spatially Equitable} approach is used to ensure that the selected samples are distributed evenly across the geographic area. The {Consecutive Spatially Equitable} approach is demonstrated through the estimation of the {Total} {Area} of {Cultivated} {Land} in {Kerman} {Province} in {Iran}. The {Consecutive Spatially Equitable} approach is shown to be more accurate than the {Consecutive} and {Spatially Equitable} approaches in this context. The {Consecutive Spatially Equitable} approach is also compared with the {Two-Stage} sampling approach, with the results showing that the {Consecutive Spatially Equitable} approach is more accurate than the {Two-Stage} approach in this context.

Unusually, few eye-in-hand camera calibration methods exist that utilize only a single video frame. Such an approach would enable the correction of camera calibration issues based on footage captured by the device itself, eliminating the need for specialized calibration tools or elaborate procedures. Although this concept is straightforward, executing it poses a complex challenge due to the eye-in-hand scenario's inherent ambiguity. This paper presents the first eye-in-hand single-frame camera calibration method from an image. We present results from experiments conducted with both simulated images and images captured from real images.

When solving inverse problems, we aim to recover an unknown image from limited and noisy observations. A common issue in this process is that there can be multiple images that lead to the same observations, making it difficult to find a solution that makes sense in the context of the problem. One approach to this challenge is conditional sampling, where we have access to prior information about the distribution of the unknown image and can generate conditioned samples based on the observations. This paper presents a new method for conditioned sampling called CREG, which uses a novel technique to smooth out the condition we are given and allows CREG to converge to a desired solution. CREG was tested on two common imaging problems, deblurring and compressed sensing, and showed promising results in generating conditioned samples that are similar to the desired images.
This research investigates the possibility of invariant surfaces in dynamical systems that are defined by fractional order.

Next-generation wireless communication systems are set to utilize terahertz frequency bands to significantly boost data transfer rates, but the high susceptibility of these signals to signal loss necessitates the adoption of multi-hop transmission methods. In this paper, we delve into the challenges of beam training in terahertz multi-hop links and propose a new approach that employs a limited number of hops to achieve reliable communication, coupled with a reinforcement learning-based method for identifying optimal beams between each hop. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in achieving high link reliability with a reduced beam training overhead, outperforming traditional methods that rely on fixed numbers of hops. Furthermore, we show that our reinforcement learning-based approach can dynamically adjust the number of hops to optimize performance.

The interstellar medium's impact on radio pulsar signals can be used to study the galaxy's radio environment. By analyzing the scintillation of the bright pulsar B133+16, researchers have identified 11 regions of the Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds with varying levels of electron density. They found that the regions with high electron density tend to have a higher concentration of HII regions, suggesting a correlation between the two. Furthermore, they found that the regions with high electron density have a higher level of Faraday rotation, suggesting a correlation between the two. They also found that the regions with high electron density have a higher level of Hα emission, suggesting a correlation between the two. They also found that the regions with high electron density have a higher level of CO emission, suggesting a correlation between the two. They also found that the regions with high electron density have a higher level of H2 emission, suggesting a correlation between the two. They also found that the regions with high electron density have a higher level of H3 emission, suggesting a correlation between the two. They also found that the regions with high electron density have a higher level of H4 emission, suggesting a correlation between the two. They also found that the regions with high electron density have a higher level of H5 emission, suggesting a correlation between the two. They also found that the regions with high electron density have a higher level of H6 emission, suggesting a correlation between the two.

To create high-quality synthetic audio that mimics real biological sounds, accurately replicating the nuances of the waveform is crucial. Current text-to-audio models, primarily based on Mel-spectrograms, struggle to produce realistic audio due to a lack of phase information. This paper introduces Quasi-Periodic WaveNet, a text-to-audio generative model that operates directly on raw audio data. It introduces a novel dilated convolution neural network that mimics the quasi-periodic characteristics of biological sounds, utilizing a combination of linear and non-linear components. This model leverages input text information to dynamically adjust the non-linear component, enabling it to learn complex sound features. Experiments conducted on three datasets - MS-COCO captions, MusicCaps, and the MS-MARCO video dataset - demonstrate that Quasi-Periodic WaveNet outperforms existing text-to-audio models in terms of similarity to the original audio waveform.

Arabic is a widely spoken language in the region, known for its rich literary history. However, a lack of annotated corpora in Arabic hinders natural language processing (NLP) research in the field. Collaborative annotation platforms can accelerate the creation of annotated datasets, which are crucial for NLP studies. MADARi, a web-based application, facilitates collaborative annotation of textual data, specifically tailored for Arabic NLP studies. It offers features such as real-time annotation, access to pre-made datasets, and integrated tools to aid annotators. The platform's capabilities are demonstrated through its use in creating the Annotated Literary Corpus of Al-Maani, a modern classical poem by a renowned Saudi poet.

This lecture will discuss the photochemistry and spectral characteristics of temperate, gas-dense exoplanets, taking into account their high densities and thermal radiation, as well as their high rates of chemical reactions and the presence of haze. Initially, we will examine the fundamental aspects of photochemistry and spectral analysis, and then delve into specific examples of temperate and gas-dense exoplanets, including hot Jupiters, super-Earths, and temperate mini-Neptunes. We will also highlight the critical role that photochemistry plays in shaping the atmospheres of these exoplanets.

To confirm the topological nature of superconducting gap in a topological superconductor through tunneling spectroscopy, distinguishing the topological Majorana zero mode peak from other peaks is essential. A practical method to achieve this involves utilizing a circuit with positive resistance, where the conductance peak of the Majorana mode remains unaffected by the resistance, while other peaks are suppressed due to their exponential dependence on the conductance. A circuit model based on a Luttinger liquid and a mean-field description of a topological superconductor demonstrates this behavior, showing that non-exponential conductance features arise from the g=0 channel and that the peak width is determined by the temperature and the energy gap, not the dissipation. Furthermore, a realistic setup using an InAs nanowire with a superconducting Al layer and a tunable tunnel barrier is proposed to experimentally verify this theory.

As urbanization increases, so does the number of road accidents, prompting a need for efficient methods to identify and address road defects. While existing techniques for detecting these flaws have their limitations, a more effective solution is required. This paper introduces RoadAtlas, a cutting-edge system built on Azure that automates road flaw detection and asset management through the use of computer vision and Azure Cognitive Services. By integrating this technology with Azure DevOps, RoadAtlas enables the creation of interactive maps that pinpoint defects and facilitate data visualization through tools like PowerBI.

This paper introduces an exhaustive breakdown of the necessary and sufficient conditions for a functor to have a bicategorical limit, specifically for functors that can be shadowed by an object within a 2-categorical framework. Additionally, we provide a detailed examination of various instances of such bicategorical constructions, including bicategorical colimits, marksmans, and throw-ins, along with relevant references to corresponding concepts in ordinary categorical theory.

This research proposes a fresh perspective on sound localization, shifting away from conventional methods. Unlike typical approaches, our method deliberately introduces deliberate distortions into the reconstruction process, resulting in a more sound-localized output. The problem is formulated as a point-cloud optimization task, with the objective of minimizing the distance between a transformed, intentionally distorted sound and its target position. The transformation is modeled using a Ray-Tracing algorithm, which simulates how a sound wave propagates through space. The optimization problem is then solved using the Iterative Closest Point method. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through the localization of a sound source in a real-world scenario.

We introduce a novel type of graph neural network called Lorentzian Graph Neural Networks (LGNNs), which utilize a signature $(1,d)$ in a Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{1+d}$ to model relational data. Many real-world datasets, such as citation networks and co-authorship graphs, naturally form a Lorentzian structure when nodes are mapped to a Euclidean space. LGNNs take advantage of this inherent property to better capture complex dependencies between data points. We propose an LGNN framework and an LGNN module that can be used with existing GNNs to leverage Lorentzian structures. Our method achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art GNN baselines on various benchmark datasets.

The primary objective of this research is to address the challenges of estimating structural dynamics from acoustic measurements. We develop a mathematical model that describes the interaction between a structure and a fluid, and derive its corresponding engagement matrix. By analyzing this matrix, we derive a key property that characterizes the system. However, solving the inverse problem presents significant challenges due to the loss of rank in the engagement matrix. We formulate the inverse problem as a minimization task and apply the alternating direction method of multipliers to derive an iterative solution. Numerical simulations are used to validate the proposed method and demonstrate its effectiveness. Additionally, an infinite-dimensional extension of the system is considered, and an extended algorithm is proposed. Numerical simulations for this case also yield positive results.

We have developed a theory for the propagation of squeezed light in an isolated, steady-state optomechanical setup. Our research indicates that, in a standard, linear optomechanical system, the interaction between the optical and mechanical components can lead to the generation of squeezing in a specific direction when the optical and mechanical modes are coupled through their mutual interaction. We have also demonstrated that this internal squeezing can be used to enhance the transmission of an incoming squeezed state, and that this enhancement is most pronounced under conditions of optomechanical dark-mode operation. Our theoretical framework has been applied to an isolated cavity setup, where we have shown that the transmission of a squeezed state can be significantly enhanced, and that this enhancement is most pronounced under conditions of low frequency and low power. Our research provides a theoretical basis for the use of optomechanical systems in the generation and manipulation of squeezed states, and has important implications for the development of quantum technologies based on steady-state entanglement.

We develop an advanced version of modal $\mu$-calculus that can effectively characterize the logic of perfect recall in both its modal and Kripke-style formulations. This enhanced calculus, which is available in both its scalar and vectorial versions, builds upon existing techniques by integrating additional modal operators and complex expressions. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through a successful translation of the logic of program equivalence with multiple visits, which was previously accomplished through the use of the scalar $\mu$-calculus.

The conventional delay devaluation model is being supplanted by a new approach, a Tsallis-inspired exponential function, which more accurately reflects the decline in user engagement over time on social media platforms. This new function incorporates a parameter that reflects the varying rates of user activity decline, reflecting the platform's characteristics. Our research proposes a new function and explores its implications, including a new method for estimating its parameters based on observed data. Additionally, we introduce a novel statistical framework to analyze the distribution of time intervals between user interactions. This framework enables us to derive a new theoretical average session duration and a new session duration formula based on the delay devaluation function. Our research demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach through a case study on Facebook, where our session duration estimates are more accurate than those derived from an exponential distribution. Furthermore, our proposed framework is generalizable to any function that models delay devaluation.

The relationship between $L_h$ and $L_{\hbar}$ is influenced by a dimensionless dimensionful quantity $G_h$, which is affected by the gravity constant $G$. The smallness of $G_h$ is a prerequisite for the smallness of $G$, but the reverse is not necessarily true. The relationship between the Planck mass and the harmonic length is not affected by the gravity constant $G$, but rather by the ratio $L_{\hbar}/L_h$. A signed graph consists of a regular graph with edges that are color-coded as either 1 or -1. The concept of graph homomorphism into signed graphs extends that of homomorphism into ordinary graphs. We investigate the critical properties of signed complete graphs, specifically those with equal amounts of 1 and -1 colored edges in the case of even-degree complete graphs. We establish a new expanded double cover technique to characterize the limit of such graphs in terms of a tuple of ordinary graph limits. This new characterization enables us to identify the minimum entropy of such graphs and determine the relationship between graph entropy and a parameter known as the chromatic entropy. Our research also uncovers the exact values of minimum entropy for graphs with certain entropy values and chromatic numbers.

The canonical average of a specific operator in a system at thermal equilibrium can be expressed as the system's total number of particles multiplied another system's specific chemical potential. This relationship can be represented using Weyl-Wigner depiction, where the canonical average of the system's chemical potential equals its total number of particles. This equality holds true for various systems, including Fermi-Dirac and Bose-Einstein systems, as well as systems described by Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics.

The concept of negative absolute temperature has been theoretically predicted and experimentally demonstrated in a few systems, prompting some physicists to view negative temperature as a valid, novel state above infinite temperature. However, we argue that this interpretation is too hasty. The established definition of temperature is based on the inverse change in entropy with respect to energy, which can yield negative values in systems with inverted population distributions. We believe declaring the negativity of temperature at this point is premature, as the current definition of temperature may not be comprehensive enough.

Let G be an abelian group and A a non-empty subset of G. For any integer k greater than one, the k-fold sumset of A, denoted as kA, is the set formed by all possible sums of k elements from A. This paper focuses on a specific subset of m-tuples (a_1,...,a_m) from A^m where the product of (a_i-a_j) for 1≤i<j≤m equals a given element d in G. We establish a lower bound for this subset when d is not zero, and under certain conditions, an exact value is established. Additionally, for a particular case where m equals three and d is zero, a bound is established for a relevant subset of A^3.

UniToPatho is a comprehensive dataset comprising 10,518 histopathological images, which are annotated at the pixel level and categorized into 10 classes. These images are derived from 8,191 slides and are used for the diagnosis and grading of colorectal polyps. Histopathological images are a critical tool in medical diagnosis, where a pathologist examines the cellular structure of a tissue sample to determine the presence of a disease. However, the process of creating such a dataset is a complex and time-consuming task, which involves the selection of relevant samples, the annotation of the images, and the categorization of the samples into relevant classes. UniToPatho is a significant contribution to the field of medical diagnosis, as it provides a comprehensive and annotated dataset that can be used to train and evaluate machine learning algorithms for the classification of tissue samples. The dataset is publicly available, which will enable researchers to develop and test new approaches for the diagnosis and grading of colorectal polyps, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

For electromagnetic diffusion issues with time-harmonic characteristics, a complex wavenumber $k$ signifies the frequency of the problem. When the domain's size is comparable to or smaller than the associated wavelength, high-frequency issues arise. A finite element method is proposed to address this, where the element size is related to a high parameter $\tau$ representing $1/k$. By employing an adaptive technique, the method optimizes the polynomial degree $p$ and the mesh size $H$ to achieve an efficient solution with the minimal number of degrees of freedom, thereby providing an optimal solution.

The proposed mechanism of a dry inner solar system, where planetesimals accumulated with a water content, is supported by the Chelyabinsk and Benenitra meteorites. These meteorites contain the same calcium-aluminum-rich inclusions (CAIs) as other meteorites, but their ordinary chondrites have a higher water content. Analysis of oxygen isotopes in these meteorites' chondrules and CAIs indicates that their water content was present in the form of water, not hydroxyl or molecular hydrogen. This observation is supported by a new model of planetesimal formation that accounts for the water content found in these meteorites. The model suggests that the early solar system's planetesimals formed in a state of humid accumulation, where they retained their water content. This model is based on the physical properties of planetesimals and their interaction with the solar system's gas and dust. Using the quantum-group symmetry of the XXZ spin chain, we've derived general expressions for structure factors at non-zero wave vectors in the solvable sectors of the model. This work extends previous studies that were limited to the nearest-neighbor interaction and a specific spin-singlet state. Our analysis covers an arbitrary spin chain system and wave vector, revealing that the structure factors can be expressed as weighted sums of conserved-spin expectations, whose values can be calculated through the Thermodynamic Limit using the TQFT. Our findings indicate that the underlying set of conserved charges is linked to the lattice's structure and that the values of these charges dictate the structure factors' behavior. This relationship becomes particularly evident in the case of spin pairs, where the TQFT values of the lattice's conserved charges directly influence the structure factors. This insight allows us to predict the spin pair oscillation pattern in the TQFT, as observed in NMR experiments.

This zero-shot voice interpretation technique enables a target language to be
achieved without the need for a corresponding keyboard input. Unlike previous
zero-shot methods that relied on pre-trained voice translation models, our approach
uses text translation and voice generation based on the corresponding text
translation. This approach allows for a wider range of target languages to be
reached. Experimental results show that our method outperforms the current zero-shot
voice translation approach and achieves a new state-of-the-art result in the
Japanese-to-Korean language translation.

In the context of electromagnetic wave interactions with spherical objects, we have derived precise formulas for scattering coefficients using a series expansion based on the reduced wavenumber and the series coefficients can be efficiently computed. Our new expressions for total scattering cross section and total field in an arbitrary direction offer accurate results, even in the direction of the incident wave, and enable accurate calculation of the Rayleigh ratio and the g-factor, which characterizes the angular distribution of scattered light. These calculations are applicable to a wide range of materials and can be utilized to design and analyze the scattering properties of complex, composite structures, such as those composed of multiple layers or made from metamaterials.

This study introduces immanant-like functions tied to Young tableaux and demonstrates that for any box filling, the Capelli double Young immanant equals the Schur altered symmetric function. A key finding reveals the equality of immanants and altered symmetric functions under specific conditions, namely when the underlying group is Young. Additionally, the Double Young immanant is shown to be expressible as a linear combination of immanants with Young determinants as coefficients. This relation is further refined to establish the immanant with Capelli double Young tables as the sum of immanants with ordinary Young tables, meeting certain determinant conditions. Moreover, the connection between Double Young matrices and the dual of the symmetric group is explored.

Within the simplest scoto-seesaw model, we examine the possible dark matter (DM) particle mass ranges and associated experimental observables, as well as the stability of the electroweak symmetry-breaking vacuum. Utilizing the neutrino mass and mixing data, we determine the minimal and maximum possible masses for the lightest new neutral particle, which is responsible for DM. We also investigate the impact of DM on the potential and estimate the mass of the lightest DM particle that maintains the robustness of the DM sector. We also consider constraints from direct DM detection experiments and future colliders. We find that, for a given neutrino mass matrix texture, the mass of the lightest new neutral particle is limited to approximately 10 GeV, while for another texture, the limit is around 100 GeV. We also determine that, for a given value of the DM mass, the self-coupling of the scalar field is within the range expected for a DM-stable and a robust vacuum. The concept of spin-orbit coupling has gained significant attention in recent years, particularly in materials with strong electron-electron interactions. In this study, we develop a unified framework to describe the hybridization between adjacent electron clouds in transition metal compounds, which can be categorized into three types: (i) spatial overlap-based static Coulomb exchange, (ii) virtual electron hopping-based Mott-Hubbard correlation, and (iii) the blending of orbital states. The third category, blending, is found to be the most crucial in certain compounds, especially those with expanded electron clouds in heavier 4d and 5d transition metals. We derive a formula for the energy scale of this phenomenon, which is determined by the difference between the on-site Coulomb interaction and the Mott-Hubbard correlation. This parameter is found to be the most critical in controlling the physical properties of these compounds, which can be described by a new effective Hamiltonian. The effective Hamiltonian's strength is determined by the spin-orbit coupling constant and the difference between the on-site Coulomb interaction and the Mott-Hubbard correlation. This framework is applied to several compounds, including Ba$_2$IrO$_4$, Sr$_2$RuO$_4$, and LaNiO$_3$, to illustrate the importance of the Hamiltonian's parameters in controlling the physical properties of these materials.

Li and Zhang previously established the fact that relative quantum homology remains invariant under rational transformations, building on a concept first introduced by Givental. This work extends their research by exploring a broader class of relations between divisors, and proving the invariance of relative quantum homology under a broader class of rational transformations.

This research proposes a novel approach to altering medical images, specifically X-rays, to convey various diseases.  Our method employs a combination of Generative Adversarial Networks and ResNet to generate specific pathological features, such as pneumonia or tuberculosis, within healthy images.  To achieve this, we utilized publicly available datasets containing images of both healthy lungs and those affected by tuberculosis and pneumonia.  Experimental results demonstrate our method's effectiveness in successfully inserting different diseases into healthy X-rays, with lower error rates compared to alternative methods.  Additionally, our approach was tested on a dataset of mixed diseases, with results showing its capability to accurately classify modified images of different pathologies.  The proposed method has the potential to be a valuable tool for data augmentation in machine learning models and for developing illness-aware medical image simulations.

Multidimensional data is commonly used in various fields, including biology, chemistry, and medicine, to analyze complex relationships. One prevalent visualization technique is Parallel Coordinates, but it has limitations in effectively displaying certain data patterns. This study introduces an examination method that combines a 2D scatter plot and a 1D histogram to provide a more comprehensive understanding of data, particularly when examining multidimensional vectors. A significant advantage of this technique is its ability to visually represent nonlinear correlations, a frequent occurrence in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, this examination method is applied to a real-world dataset, specifically the MNIST dataset, to demonstrate its effectiveness. A significant outcome of this research is the development of a user-friendly instrument, known as ViDaExpert, which integrates both the 2D scatter plot and 1D histogram examination method into a single, easy-to-use interface.

We have developed an efficient method for rapidly computing Newtonian potentials on flat surfaces, applicable to various scenarios including calculating gravitational potentials and electric potentials. This approach leverages a straightforward and user-friendly technique, utilizing the properties of logarithmic potentials in two-dimensional space and the concept of conformal mapping. By employing this technique, we can quickly and accurately determine potentials for complex charge or mass distributions by breaking them down into smaller, more manageable components. As a result, this method offers a quick and reliable way to visualize the effects of these distributions on flat surfaces.
